data.text: The repo has no app code yet; there is no earlier stage to wait for (ignore 'Stage 1'). Use Python 3 standard library only (http.server), in hello.py at the repo root. GET /hello returns HTTP 200, Content-Type text/plain, body exactly 'hello'. Add one unittest in test_hello.py. No other files.

decisions: Add a minimal HTTP hello endpoint using only the Python 3 standard library (http.server). Create hello.py at the repo root defining a request handler (and a way to run a server) where GET /hello responds with HTTP 200, Content-Type text/plain, and a body of exactly 'hello'. Add test_hello.py at the repo root with one unittest that starts the server (e.g. on an ephemeral port in a background thread), issues GET /hello, and asserts the status, content type, and body. No other files are added or changed; there is no prior stage to wait for (the repo currently has no app code).
Per trusted human answer: stdlib http.server only, hello.py at repo root, GET /hello -> 200 text/plain body exactly 'hello', one unittest in test_hello.py, no other files.
Server binds 127.0.0.1:8000 by default, optional port as first CLI argument.
Non-/hello paths return 404 via send_error; Content-Length: 5 is sent.
Test binds port 0 and runs the server in a daemon thread to avoid port clashes and hangs.
lessons_proposed: CI in this repo runs 'echo tests ok' and process.yaml is protected, so state in the spec that unit tests must be run by hand in UAT rather than relying on CI.
